harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent OpenLDAP field-level privacy on node1 and verified it from node2. Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery checks without changing CentOS 5.11 or kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
actions_performed: Loaded the supplied HR LDIF and retained the original file and checksum.
Provisioned generated, root-protected reader and HR administrator credentials.
Configured ACLs so the reader sees names and mail but not employeeNumber; only the administrator can read or change employeeNumber.
Blocked anonymous employee access and restricted LDAP network access to node2.
Verified reader denial, administrator modification, restoration of HR-4815, and anonymous isolation.
Rebooted node2 and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Supplied LDIF loaded into LDAP on node1
evidence.summary: Direct administrator searches show Morgan Lake, morgan@hr.test, and employeeNumber HR-4815 before and after node1's restart.

evidence.requirement: Reader can search names and mail from node2 but cannot read employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Reader searches from node2 return cn, sn, and mail while omitting employeeNumber, including after both restarts.

evidence.requirement: Only HR administrator may read or change employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Reader modifications fail with LDAP error 50. The administrator successfully changed the value, restored HR-4815, and retained read access after restart.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous users see no employee records
evidence.summary: Anonymous employee searches return zero entries before and after restart.
Generated reader and administrator credential files are root-owned, mode 600, and persisted on both relevant nodes; no secret values were exposed.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.

Healthy baseline boot ID e8429694-dad0-4d03-8000-000000000000, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID d9ea2148-7a21-419a-8000-000000000000, and recovered reader/anonymous behavior are directly shown.

Healthy baseline boot ID 237b45d6-a48e-48ce-8000-000000000000, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID fcb107a1-913d-46ec-8000-000000000000, automatic slapd recovery, retained data/ACL/firewall state, and successful end-to-end access are directly shown.
